review_method: Fresh visual inspection of the retained original map pixels, cartographic credits, successful original acquisition receipt and official discovery record. Every selected source and baseline-rendered polygon part and ring was viewed in full; all ordered positions, bounds and ring closure were independently recomputed from the retained source collection and selected decoded baseline. Regional position, orientation, complete outline, named water labels and narrow connections were considered together; neither bounds nor label overlap alone established identity. The packed decoder was not independently replayed by this reviewer. Independent observations were recorded before comparing the source researcher’s draft.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory lake target IDs; repeated map labels do not increase the target count.

findings.follow_up_scope: Resolve the Nuyakuk–Tikchik inter-lake and connecting-neck name boundary with more detailed direct evidence before any separately authorized scalar naming or geometric subdivision. No split line or geometry repair is proposed here.
findings.supported_name_scope: The complete generalized selected footprint in the Wood-Tikchik region contains western and central water labelled Nuyakuk Lake and eastern water labelled Tikchik Lake. They are distinct component associations, not aliases or alternative scalar names for the whole polygon. The single selected ring crosses two separately labelled lakes and their connecting neck; no exact inter-lake partition is established, and fine western bays and eastern outlet detail are generalized. Exact extent and product-name application are not approved.
limits: The single selected ring crosses two separately labelled lakes and their connecting neck; no exact inter-lake partition is established, and fine western bays and eastern outlet detail are generalized.
Lake Chauekuktuli is a separate water to the north. Tikchik Lodge is a landmark, not an additional lake name or a precise name-boundary marker.
The direct evidence is one Alaska DNR-hosted third-party TOPO! map, not a formal government naming registry or independently corroborated naming decision.
No alternate word order, additional alias or Korean form is certified.
